title: Arcaded Squares of South Bohemia

bestPeriod.note: State chateaux shut from November to March and open weekends only in April and October; late October brings the Třeboň pond harvests.

summary: Three arcaded Renaissance squares in seven days, Krumlov, Třeboň and Telč, with carp ponds, a Baroque theatre and two long lie-ins.
hook: South Bohemia is a landscape of engineered water and unhurried squares. Three towns, two short drives, and a week spent walking arcades that have not changed shape since a fire in 1530 forced the rebuild. Nothing here needs to be rushed, and most of it closes on Mondays anyway.

snapshot.Base(s): Český Krumlov (3 nights) · Třeboň (2 nights) · Telč (2 nights)
snapshot.Total Distance / Terrain: Approx. 260 km of driving across the whole week, all on flat to gently rolling secondary roads; 30-35 km walked
snapshot.Getting There: Fly to Prague (PRG); direct coach to Český Krumlov in approx. 3h, or hire a car at the airport
snapshot.Who It Suits: Architecture readers, slow eaters, families, anyone who wants UNESCO towns without Prague's crowds

itinerary.title: Into the Vltava bend
itinerary.morning: Collect a car at Prague airport, or take the direct RegioJet coach south; either way you are in Český Krumlov in about three hours. The old town sits inside a tight double loop of the Vltava, and cars stay outside it.
itinerary.afternoon: Walk náměstí Svornosti, the small sloping main square with its 1716 plague column and Renaissance town hall arcade, then follow Horní to the church of St Vitus and back down Latrán, the trade street under the castle wall.
itinerary.evening: Eat early. The Eggenberg brewery has been working below the castle since the 16th century and its beer is the local pour. Then walk the riverbank after dark, when the town lights the castle tower and empties out.
itinerary.dayStats: Towns visited: 1. Walking: 5 km. Transfer time: approx. 3h from Prague.

itinerary.title: Monday rules, so walk
itinerary.morning: Nothing before 10:00. Czech state monuments close on Mondays, which makes this a day for streets rather than interiors. Cross the Plášťový most, the covered cloak bridge spanning the moat on three tiers of arches, and walk the castle gardens instead.
itinerary.afternoon: The Klášter complex, the former Minorite and Poor Clares monasteries on Klášterní, runs working craft workshops where you can watch, and often try, hand papermaking, blacksmithing and pottery. The marionette makers' shops on and around Radniční are the other Krumlov craft to look at properly: carved limewood heads, painted, strung by hand.
itinerary.evening: Dinner on Parkán, the lane along the river below the square. The Egon Schiele Art Centrum on Široká stays open some Mondays; check the board on your way past.
itinerary.dayStats: Towns visited: 1. Walking: 7 km. Transfer time: none.

itinerary.title: Castle, theatre, monastery
itinerary.morning: The Zámek Český Krumlov guided routes reopen today. Route I covers the Renaissance and Baroque state rooms; the Baroque Theatre of 1766 is a separate, tightly capped tour and it is the reason to be here. Original stage machinery, painted flats, thunder run and wind machine, all still worked by rope. Tours run roughly May to October and sell out days ahead, book online.
itinerary.afternoon: Drive 10 km north to the Cistercian monastery at Zlatá Koruna, founded 1263, whose chapterhouse is one of the finest early Gothic rooms in Bohemia. Twenty minutes of driving, an hour inside, and almost nobody there.
itinerary.evening: Back in Krumlov, climb the castle tower before it closes for the last long view down onto the roofs.
itinerary.dayStats: Towns visited: 2. Walking: 6 km. Transfer time: 40 min return by car.

itinerary.title: Folk baroque and the pond town
itinerary.morning: Another slow start; nothing before 10:00. Then drive 20 km northeast to Holašovice, a UNESCO village whose green is ringed by 23 farmsteads with the curved, whitewashed, ornamented gables of *selské baroko*, south Bohemian rural baroque. It takes half an hour and it is unlike anything else in Europe.
itinerary.afternoon: Continue 55 km east to Třeboň, arriving mid-afternoon. Masarykovo náměstí is a long arcaded rectangle of gabled burgher houses; the Bílý koníček on the corner has carried its date of 1544 through everything since.
itinerary.evening: Carp is not a joke here, it is the local farmed fish and it is properly cooked. Order it grilled or *na černo* and follow it with Regent, brewed in the town since 1379.
itinerary.dayStats: Towns visited: 3. Walking: 4 km. Transfer time: approx. 1h30 driving.

itinerary.title: Engineered water
itinerary.morning: The Třeboň basin is a 16th-century fish-farming machine. Walk the dam of Rybník Svět straight out of town, then into the woods to the Schwarzenberg mausoleum, a neo-Gothic tomb standing alone above the water. Circuit of the lake: about 12 km, entirely flat; the short version to the mausoleum and back is 5 km.
itinerary.afternoon: Drive 15 km to the dam of Rybník Rožmberk, the largest pond in the country at 489 hectares, dug out between 1584 and 1590 by the estate engineer Jakub Krčín. The Zlatá stoka, the 45 km Golden Canal that feeds the whole system, was cut even earlier. If you are here in late October or early November, ask locally about the *výlov*, the pond harvest, when the water is drawn down and the carp are netted in front of a crowd.
itinerary.evening: Třeboň is a peat spa town; Bertiny lázně takes walk-ins for peat wraps. Otherwise, arcades and a beer.
itinerary.dayStats: Towns visited: 1. Walking: 9 km. Transfer time: 40 min return by car.

itinerary.title: Nativity figures and a narrow gauge
itinerary.morning: Drive 30 km northeast to Jindřichův Hradec. náměstí Míru is a broad arcaded square with a Trinity column; the castle behind it holds the Rondel, a free-standing Renaissance garden pavilion with a stucco ceiling that stops conversation.
itinerary.afternoon: The Muzeum Jindřichohradecka holds Krýzovy jesličky, a mechanical folk nativity built over sixty years by a local stocking-maker: nearly 1,400 figures, over 130 of them moving. If the 760 mm narrow-gauge line to Nová Bystřice is running a steam day, take that instead.
itinerary.evening: Continue 30 km to Telč and check in on the square. Arrive in time to see it empty at dusk.
itinerary.dayStats: Towns visited: 3. Walking: 5 km. Transfer time: approx. 1h20 driving.

itinerary.title: Telč, arcade by arcade
itinerary.morning: náměstí Zachariáše z Hradce is a long triangular space enclosed by continuous arcades and about forty gabled houses, each front different, rebuilt in Renaissance dress after the 1530 fire. Farmers' markets set up here on Saturday mornings, roughly 08:00-12:00, from spring to autumn, bread, honey, smoked fish, and Vysočina cheese.
itinerary.afternoon: The Státní zámek Telč tour takes in the Golden Hall with its coffered ceiling of thirty painted panels. Afterwards walk the causeway between the Štěpnický and Ulický ponds that make the town an island. If you have time before flying, Slavonice is 30 km south and its squares are covered in 16th-century sgraffito.
itinerary.evening: Telč to Prague airport is about 2h15 by road.
itinerary.dayStats: Towns visited: 2. Walking: 5 km. Transfer time: approx. 2h15 to Prague.

accommodationStrategy.name: Hotel Konvice
accommodationStrategy.description: On Horní, a minute from náměstí Svornosti and directly above the river bend, with rooms looking across to the castle. Small, old, wooden-floored, and inside the pedestrian zone, which matters, because the old town is closed to cars and this end of it has the shortest walk in from the parking areas.
accommodationStrategy.booking: 6-8 weeks ahead for May, June and September.

accommodationStrategy.name: Bílý koníček
accommodationStrategy.description: The oldest surviving house on Masarykovo náměstí, working as a modest hotel with a restaurant under the arcade. You are on the square, inside the walls, five minutes from the Svět dam walk and the Regent brewery gate, the two things you came to Třeboň for. Parking is outside the historic core.
accommodationStrategy.booking: 4-6 weeks ahead; longer if you come for the pond harvest.

accommodationStrategy.name: Hotel Celerin
accommodationStrategy.description: Twelve or so rooms directly on náměstí Zachariáše z Hradce, several facing the arcades. Being on the square is the whole point in Telč: day visitors arrive at 10:00 and are gone by 17:00, and the hours either side belong to whoever sleeps here. Ask for a front room and accept the church bells.
accommodationStrategy.booking: 6 weeks ahead, more for summer weekends.

logistics.emergency: 112 works everywhere. Czech services direct: 155 ambulance, 158 police, 150 fire.
logistics.money: Czechia uses the koruna, not the euro. Decline dynamic currency conversion, and withdraw from bank ATMs rather than the independent machines in tourist streets.

other.label: Motorway vignette
other.text: A digital vignette (*dálniční známka*) is required on Czech motorways and is bought online at edalnice.cz against your plate; a ten-day one costs roughly CZK 270. Class II and III roads, most of this route, are free, and confirm with the rental desk whether a vignette is already registered.

other.label: Monday closures
other.text: State castles and chateaux, including Český Krumlov, Jindřichův Hradec and Telč, close on Mondays. They also close entirely from November to March and run weekends only in April and October.

other.label: Guided-tour language
other.text: Chateau tours run in Czech by default; English slots are fixed-time or need a minimum group. Book the English slot online.

other.label: Parking
other.text: All three old towns restrict traffic. Use the signed car parks outside the walls, roughly CZK 50-100 per day, and tip about 10% in restaurants as you pay.

other.label: Opening-hour traps
other.text: Small-town Czech kitchens stop serving hot food around 21:00, and many close one weekday. Museums often shut for lunch between 12:00 and 13:00.

proTips: Book the Krumlov Baroque Theatre as soon as your dates are fixed. Capacity is tiny, the season short, and nothing else on this itinerary substitutes for it.
Krumlov's castle courtyards stay open long after the ticketed routes close. Walk them at 21:00, with no tour groups anywhere.
The Svět circuit is best walked anti-clockwise in the afternoon so the low sun is behind you over the water on the return leg.
Buy smoked carp fillets from the fish counter on Masarykovo náměstí and eat them on the dam. It is what Třeboň people do and it costs almost nothing.
Telč's square photographs badly at midday and beautifully at 07:30, when the arcades are in shadow and the gables catch the light.
If the weather collapses, Slavonice's houses hide rib-vaulted interiors and the town runs tours of its medieval underground passages.

packingNotes: Comfortable shoes with a real sole: every square on this trip is cobbled and cambered.
A warm layer for evenings, the Vysočina plateau around Telč sits at 500 m and drops sharply after sunset even in June.
Insect repellent for the Třeboň wetlands from June to August. Mosquitoes there are serious.
Cash in koruna, around CZK 2,000, for markets, car parks and village pubs.
Offline maps and a light rain jacket: Vysočina signal is patchy and the pond basin makes its own weather.
whatCouldGoWrong: **You arrive on a Monday and everything is shut.** This itinerary assumes it. If your dates shift, move the walking day onto whichever day is Monday.
**The Baroque Theatre is sold out.** No substitute exists, but Krumlov's castle Route II and the Museum Fotoatelier Seidel, a preserved 1900s photographic studio on Linecká, fill the slot well.
**Rain for a full day.** Třeboň's spa, the Regent brewery tour, the Jindřichův Hradec museum and Krumlov's monastery workshops are all indoors.
**Your car is ticketed in an old town.** The zones are enforced; if your hotel sits inside one, have them register your plate for loading access before you drive in.
